note: Grade 3 addsub builds 12 stacked addition and subtraction problems with 3-digit numbers, sums kept within 1000, any method fits the work space; the estimate check is not printed, the teacher can ask for it.

Grade 3 compare makes pairs with the same numerator or the same denominator, each drawn as two equal bars to shade and compare with <, > or =; count l gives 10 pairs (closest to 12); the written reason is not prompted but the bars are the reason.
Grade 3 compo draws 6 L-shaped figures with all six sides labeled and asks for the area; the key and teacher page show the split-into-rectangles or big-minus-small working.
Grade 4 addsub stacks 12 problems with 4- and 5-digit numbers in standard-algorithm layout; regroup=with makes every problem regroup, though regrouping across zeros is not guaranteed on every sheet.
Grade 4 mul gives 12 stacked problems (2-digit by 2-digit and up to 4-digit by 1-digit) with space to write partial products; the estimate check on 3 of them is not printed.

Grade 4 div gives 12 long-division bracket problems, 3- and 4-digit dividends by 1-digit divisors with remainders written as R; partial quotients fit the bracket layout, drawings are the student's own.
Grade 4 mixed adds and subtracts mixed numbers with like denominators, 12 problems (closest to 10), answers in simplest mixed form and worked steps on the teacher page including regrouping a whole.
Grade 4 missing gives 9 text problems (closest to 8): a rectangle with a given area or perimeter and one side, find the other side; key shows the working.
Grade 5 mul stacks 12 problems of 3-digit by 2-digit numbers for the standard algorithm; the estimate check is not printed.
Grade 5 div gives 12 long-division problems, 4-digit dividends by 2-digit divisors (11 to 49), remainders as R; the bracket layout takes partial quotients, area models are the student's own.
Grade 5 addunlike adds and subtracts fractions with unlike denominators (LCD at most 60), 12 problems, steps on the teacher page show the renaming; about 3 in 10 involve a mixed number.
Grade 5 volc draws 6 solids made of two joined boxes (an L in front view) with all dimensions labeled; the key adds the two prism volumes.
Grade 7 ineq2 gives 8 two-step inequalities with a blank number line under each; coefficients range over negatives so some flip the sign, and the key graphs each answer.
Grade 8 dist gives 8 equations of the form p(x + q) = r that need the distributive property, with integer (so rational) coefficients and stepwise solutions on the teacher page.
Crossword built from the Life Cycles Word Wall with meanings as clues; 10 words (the largest count) instead of 12, and the order-a-scrambled-cycle extra is not made.
Grade 3 claim-evidence-reasoning frame (question, claim, two evidence boxes, reasoning, conclusion) with the meerkat question as the printed prompt.
Grade 4 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with the cactus prompt printed; students supply the two structures as evidence.
Grade 3-5 science observation log: prediction line plus four dated observation boxes with a drawing space, one per week, and two reflection prompts.
Grade 5 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with the sun-brightness question as the printed prompt.
Single-trait complete-dominance crosses with real traits; students fill each square and give genotype and phenotype ratios plus one probability. Four crosses per sheet (the largest count), not eight.
Two-circle Venn labeled Sexual and Asexual with a sum-it-up box; students add their own organism examples in the circles.

Grade 9-12 science log: hypothesis, independent, dependent and controlled variable boxes, a trial data table, sketch or graph space and a sources-of-error box; the student names the one variable tested.
Grade 9 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with alternate explanation, rebuttal and limitations; the topic prompt asks for the feedback and its evidence.
Grade 9 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with the pocket mouse prompt; variation, inheritance, selection and time go in the reasoning section.

Grade 3 map-skills draws one map with a lettered-and-numbered grid, a compass rose with NE/SE/SW/NW, a key and a scale bar (1 square = 100 m), then asks about 8 questions that use all four: what is in a square, which square a place is in, cardinal and intermediate directions, a scale distance, a route and a draw-a-star. Only gap: the map is a made-up town, not a state map, and the row says 10 questions.

Grade 8 argument frame (2-page drafting space) with the claim printed as the topic: introduction with claim, Body 1 and Body 2 reason-evidence-explanation, Body 3 opposing claim answered with evidence, conclusion, plus a linking-word bank and a standards checklist. Gap: two evidence bodies instead of three, and the sheet does not reference the corkboard from row 35.

12 missing-number equations within 20 with the unknown in either operand spot (? + 8 = 11 and 8 + ? = 11, plus subtraction forms); the key shows the undo step. Does not reverse the equal sign as in 5 = ? - 3.
10 shaded bars; each asks either k/d = ? copies of 1/d or k copies of 1/d = ?, so students name the shaded fraction as copies of a unit fraction.
Picture graph of Books Read This Month where each book icon stands for 5, with read, most/fewest, how-many-more, together, total and two-step comparison questions.
9 rectangles and L-shapes drawn on a grid of unit squares; students count squares and answer in square units (row asks for 8; 9 is the nearest count).
6 division stories that each leave a remainder; directions tell students to say what the remainder means: round up, drop it or report it.
8 add and subtract problems with mixed numbers and unlike denominators; the checker requires a mixed number with unlike denominators and the key covers regrouping when the fraction part is larger.
First-quadrant plane, two pages of 8 items each split between naming lettered points and plotting given points (8 plot, 8 name; row says 10 and 6).
12 expressions with whole-number exponents evaluated by the order of operations; every answer is a whole number and the key shows the exponent step first.
12 items alternating expand and factor with the distributive property (6 of each), factoring out the greatest common factor like 4x - 12 = 4(x - 3).

12 both-sides equations, about a third each with one solution, no solution and identity; students solve and write x = n, no solution or all real numbers (row asks for 10; 12 is the nearest option after 8).
Compare chart with the three organisms as typed column headers and the four life stages as typed row labels; the grade 3-5 chart adds a Same or different column.
Grade 3 bar graph of six animal life spans from custom data; the questions read, compare and add values and the last asks for a reason.
T-chart sort with the two headers and a cut-out strip of ten trait cards (the row's four plus six more of the same kind).
Design planner has the problem, criteria, constraints, three ideas, a labeled sketch of the chosen idea, a materials list and a test plan; covers the sketch, materials and criteria the row asks for.
Design planner with a labeled sketch, materials and a How I will test it box; the sand tray test is what students write in that box.

Science observation log: Date, Time, Conditions, Measurement (with units) and What I observe columns with six rows, enough for five shadow readings in one day with direction in the observation column.
Design planner for grades 6-8 has criteria, constraints, three ideas, a chosen labeled sketch, materials, a test plan (what to measure and how), results and improve.
Compare chart with Fission and Fusion as columns and the row's four criteria as typed row labels, plus a Why the difference matters column; two spare rows stay blank.

Eight conservation of momentum problems: carts, train cars, clay and blocks and tackles that stick together, plus skaters, an astronaut and a cannon pushing apart from rest (explosions), with formula and worked key.
Eight problems alternating work (W = F x d: pushing boxes, lifting onto a shelf, pushing a car) and power (P = W / t: running up stairs, elevator, crane, winch), with formula, units and worked key.
Eight v = f x lambda problems on rope, spring, pool and ocean waves and sound in air at 343 m/s; no seismic context, so two of the row's three wave kinds.
Trial log with four numbered rows (Date, What I did, What I measured or saw, Notes) and a summary box; failures and the change per round go in the Notes column.
Grade 3 persuasive letter frame: opening with the problem, my idea (the fix), reason 1, reason 2, closing that asks the principal to act; the offer to help goes in the closing box.
Compare chart with Nuuk and Lagos as columns and the five rows the row names, plus a same/different column and a sum-up box.
Grade 4-5 persuasive letter frame: paragraph 1 the problem, paragraph 2 what I propose (the law), two reason paragraphs, closing ask; date and sign-off printed.
Build mode prints a 5-product table for a sample state and an empty grid; students draw the bar graph, then answer the generated reading questions. Values are invented for a made-up state.
Three-subject compare chart with the colonial regions as columns and the four rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four named people as columns and rows for role, side and reason; content comes from the module lessons.
Compare chart with the five rows the row names; the sum-up box asks which difference matters most, which is the biggest-change question.
Three-subject compare chart with the three belief systems as columns and the three rows the row names.
Three-subject compare chart for a tax, a ban and a subsidy with the who-pays and behavior rows the row names, plus one extra row.
Three-subject compare chart with the five rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four regions as columns and the four rows the row names.
Three-subject compare chart with the three compromises as columns and the three rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart of the four decision methods on speed, fairness and buy-in; the class trip scenario is the chart title.
Grade 6-8 case brief frame: facts, question, ruling, reasoning, why it matters (judicial review goes there).
Compare chart with local, state and national as columns and the five citizen tools as rows; each cell holds the historic example.
Four-subject compare chart with the four revolutions as columns and the four rows the row names.
Three-subject compare chart with the two rows the row names plus one extra row.
Three-subject compare chart with the three states as columns and the four rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four strikes as columns and the four rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four amendments as columns and the three rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four organizations as columns and the three rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four campaigns as columns and leaders, tactics and wins as rows.

The space set holds exactly 10 events from Sputnik (1957) to Apollo 11 (1969) and grade 11 sheets use 10, so the sheet sequences those 10 Soviet and US firsts with before/after and years-between questions; the Cold War stakes discussion is not on the sheet.
Three-subject compare chart with the three technologies as columns and the three rows the row names.
Grade 9-12 case brief frame: facts, question, ruling, reasoning (where the Necessary and Proper Clause reading goes), dissent or concurrence, why it matters.
Four-subject compare chart with the four systems as columns and the three economic questions as rows.
Four-subject compare chart with the four structures as columns and the rows the row names plus an example row.
Four-subject compare chart with the four institutions as columns and how-it-reduces-risk and example rows.
Three-subject compare chart with the three Fed tools as columns and how-it-works and effect rows.
Four-subject compare chart with the four methods as columns and the three rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four theories as columns and the three rows the row names.
Four-subject compare chart with the four treatments as columns and the three rows the row names.

Grade 3 opinion frame is one paragraph: opinion topic sentence, Reason 1-3 each with an example line, concluding sentence; its grade 3 transition bank is because, therefore, since, for example; checklist is W.3.1.

Grade 6 informative planning frame: Introduction with thesis, Body 1-3 (topic sentence, facts, explanation), Conclusion, on one page. Bodies are the three sections; the sheet has no printed heading line per body, so students write their own heading in the first line.

Grade 6 narrative planning frame: Exposition (narrator, point of view, characters), Rising action (dialogue and description), Climax, Falling action, Resolution and reflection; checklist is W.6.3 (sequence, dialogue, pacing, conclusion). Topic left open for a made-up narrative.
